Combat Systems

Source: DESIGN-COMBAT-STATS.md and DESIGN-BATTLE-READABILITY.md, checked against Assets/Scripts/Core/Combat/CombatSimulation.cs. Combat resolves as a pure function (CombatSimulation.Run()) that returns an ordered list of BattleEvents up front; the battle screen only plays that list back and never computes anything itself.

The damage pipeline — implemented, in order

ApplyDamageEffect resolves a hit in this order (all confirmed live in current code):

#StepWhat it does
1Basesource.EffectiveAttack * effect.Power + effect.Flat
2Aspect factormultiplies by AspectChart.Multiplier (×1.10 favoured / ×0.92 disfavoured — see Aspects)
3Passive bonus vs. statuswas Kalyx's Kindling only; now dead code since Kindling was cut
4Critrolls EffectiveCritChance, then multiplies by CritDamage
5Defencemultiplies by 1 - defense / (defense + DefenseConstant + DefensePerLevel * level)
6Damage variancemultiplies by a random spread
7Round and floorrounds away from zero, clamps up to a minimum damage
8Shield, then HPabsorbs into Shield first, remainder to HP

Worth knowing: mitigation (step 5) is multiplicative and lands after the crit multiplier, so a crit and a non-crit hit are reduced by the same fraction — Defence doesn't blunt crit spikes specifically, it scales everything equally.

The results-screen "you were the wrong colour" Debrief clause moved with the wheel narrowing and is shipped at the narrowed values today: Debrief.AspectFactorThreshold is 1.01 and Debrief.AspectDominantShare is 0.35, confirmed live in Debrief.cs. Both were re-checked against the ×1.10/×0.92 wheel above in the same pass, so the clause still fires correctly rather than silently going dark at a stale 1.2 threshold.

Defence — already existed, no change needed

The original proposal that spawned DESIGN-COMBAT-STATS.md asked for a "Defence" stat to be added to the pipeline. It was already there (EffectiveDefense on CombatUnit, folding in DefenseUp/DefenseDown with a floor), so this part of the proposal was rejected as redundant — nothing was built. Armour penetration was also considered and rejected: it would just be DefenseDown with extra steps, and the project's rule bans percentage stat sticks anyway.

Block — proposed, rejected as specified

A "chance to reduce an incoming hit" stat was proposed and rejected: its expected value reduces to a flat multiplier (exactly what the no-percentage-stat-stick rule forbids), and it's the most expensive draw to add to the highest-frequency code path in the simulation. Not built. The doc leaves the door open for a rule-shaped version later (PassiveTrigger.OnBlock making "blocks feed a counterattack" writable, or Block negating a status rider rather than a damage slice) but notes any such attempt would be competing directly with Lumen's identity and needs to be argued against it specifically. PassiveTrigger.OnBlock exists in the enum but has no implementation or content using it — see Glossary.

Effect Hit / Effect Resist — implemented

Proposed as one opposed mechanic and built. Confirmed in code: CombatSimulation.cs:ResolveLandingChance computes landing = baseChance + sourceEffectHit - targetEffectResist (additive, not multiplicative — kept additive deliberately so a point of the stat is worth the same regardless of a status's base chance), clamped, and only rolled for harmful statuses (beneficial/self-applied statuses like Taunt or Shield always apply as authored). EffectHit/EffectResist are flat stats (not scaled by level or rarity, like CritChance) read straight from each hero/enemy's JSON — see Heroes for current values.

A new BattleEventType.StatusResisted event was added (confirmed in BattleEvent.cs and emitted in CombatSimulation.cs) so a resisted debuff has a visible trace in the event record instead of just silently not appearing, and Debrief.cs reads it for the results-screen wording.

Why this mattered beyond the stat itself: without it, Umbra's uncleansable-debuff identity (see Aspects) had no counterplay at all once a debuff landed — the only lever was whether it landed, and that used to be a fixed constant nobody could influence. Effect Resist is the defender's side of that roll.

Team size 3 → 5 — implemented

Confirmed in current content and code: balance.json's maxTeamSize is 5, PlayerProfile.Team is sized to it, and CombatSimulation.BuildUnits reads _cfg.MaxTeamSize for both sides (including enemy spawns — the docs flagged this as a trap, since every stage in campaign.json needed refilling to five spawns or the enemy side would stay at three and every fight would trivially win). This work was coupled to the Effect Hit/Resist rollout because AllEnemies effects resolve once per living target, so the value of a point of Effect Hit is a direct function of team size — the docs insisted on shipping and retuning both together rather than in two separate passes.

Determinism

Combat runs on a single deterministic RNG stream (DeterministicRng, xorshift32) shared across an entire battle. Adding or removing a single draw anywhere shifts every subsequent roll for the rest of that fight — the doc leaned on this heavily to argue Effect Hit/Resist could ship in two phases: phase A (stats present, defaulted to zero, arithmetic bypassed entirely when both are zero) is provably a no-op against existing seeded battles; phase B (authoring non-zero values on real heroes/enemies) invalidates every existing win-rate table and requires a full campaign retune.

Battle readability — mostly implemented

DESIGN-BATTLE-READABILITY.md's core rule: "most of what looks missing [on the battle screen] is not missing, it is unread" — the event list already has it, the screen just needs to read it rather than recompute it. Per that doc's own inline status markers, most of its asks have been fixed: TurnStart now has a handled case, the real (not geometrically-guessed) target is resolved via event lookahead, the turn strip reads the round's TurnStart events, and both AspectFactor and AbilityName fields were added to the Damage event (read by the battle screen's WEAK/RESIST tags and by Debrief). Two items remain only partially addressed per the doc's own notes: the killer (Death.SourceId) is used in the post-battle Debrief screen but not shown inline during playback, and Ember's Burn-stacking (see Aspects) produces multiple simultaneous Burn instances that the status bar still only renders as one BRN tag — a genuine display gap, not just an unread record.
